rationale: GIL has already gapped down ~26% on fraud/accounting allegations and is now trading at 96% of today's range near the session high after recovering from $31.34 to $33.34 — the easy directional move has largely played out. The stock is pressing against today's high ($33.40) with momentum stalling (last candle volume collapsed to 9k), making a long entry at resistance risky, while shorting into a stock that has already absorbed a catastrophic gap and is showing intraday recovery momentum is equally unattractive. With a broad market selloff (SPY -3.42%, VIXY +21%) adding macro noise and the fraud narrative already priced into the gap, the risk/reward in either direction is unclear enough to warrant standing aside.
